newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PADRES SEND VAUGHN TO YANKEES FOR ROGERS AND DUNCAN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PADRES SEND VAUGHN TO YANKEES FOR ROGERS AND DUNCAN.

text.p: The Padres and New York Yankees completed an expected trade Friday night, with San Diego acquiring left-hander Kenny Rogers, infielder Mariano Duncan and a minor-league pitcher for outfielder Greg Vaughn and two minor-leaguers.

The deal had been rumoured since the middle of the week and relieves New York of two players who have been without a defined role for weeks. The trade is contingent on power-hitting Vaughn and Rogers passing physicals.

It is the second deal between the teams since the start of the season. The Padres sent Japanese pitcher Hideki Irabu to the Yankees along with three minor-leaguers in exchange for outfielder Ruben Rivera, minor-league pitcher Rafael Medina and $3 million in cash in April.

"Greg Vaughn is a class act," said San Diego president Larry Lucchino. "He will be remembered not only for helping us to the division title last year, but for his dedication and contributions to the community."

Yankees manager Joe Torre said after his team's game in Toronto against the Blue Jays: "We had to move a pitcher to make room for Irabu. In Dunc's case, it was waiting for the shoe to fall for a month, and I'm glad it finally happened."
Vaughn, who turned 32 Thursday, is hitting just .224 with 10 homers and 24 RBI in 64 games. But he had 41 home runs and 117 RBI in 145 games for Milwaukee and San Diego last season.
The Padres signed Vaughn to a three-year, $15 million contract in the off-season, but he has struggled most of the year and lost his starting left field job to Rickey Henderson.
Vaughn should provide the Yankees with right-handed power and is expected to move in as the starting left fielder.

Rogers is in the second year of a four-year, $20 million deal, but was relegated to long relief by the Yankees even before the arrival of Irabu. Rogers is 4-4 with a 5.90 ERA and was bumped from the rotation in favour of Ramiro Mendoza.
Rogers, 32, was 12-8 with a 4.68 ERA last season. Some critics questioned whether the lefty has the psychological makeup to deal with the pressures of pitching in New York.

The 34-year-old Duncan was a vital cog in New York's World Series run last year, batting a career-high .340. But his playing time was reduced this year and he asked to be traded. Duncan is batting .247 with one homer and 11 RBI in 46 games.

"It's a tough thing," Torre said. "You get close to players and things change in this game. I'll never forget what he (Duncan) meant to this club last year. He came down the bench, we had a hug goodbye."

Accompanying Vaughn to New York are minor-league pitchers Kerry Taylor and Chris Clark. Taylor, a 26-year-old right-hander, was 5-4 with a 3.63 ERA for Triple-A Las Vegas. Clark, a 22-year-old right-hander, was 1-5 with a 5.48 ERA with Clinton of the Class-A Midwest League.
Kevin Henthorne, a 27-year-old right-hander, goes to San Diego after posting a 1-0 record with a 3.58 ERA in 20 games for Double-A Norwich.
